info.name: Blogging Platform API - by User Story
info.description:
Every endpoint of blogPlatform III, grouped by user story (Epic 1 to 5).

**How to run**
1. Start the app: `mvnw spring-boot:run` (MySQL must be running). Change `baseUrl` if it is not http://localhost:8080.
2. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner, top to bottom. "US 1.1" creates the test data, "Clean up" deletes it.
3. Each run uses a new `run` id, so you can run it again and again.

Every /api response has the shape { success, status, message, data | errors, timestamp }. A collection-level test checks it on every request.

item.name: US 1.1 - Spring Data JPA integration
item.description:
**As a developer, I want to configure and integrate Spring Data JPA so that data persistence operations are simplified and consistent.**

Acceptance criteria covered:
- AC 1.1.1 Spring Data JPA added and configured
- AC 1.1.2 Entities with @Entity, @Id and relationship mappings (@ManyToOne, @OneToMany, @ManyToMany)
- AC 1.1.3 Repositories extend JpaRepository (save / findById come for free)
- AC 1.1.4 The application connects to the database

This folder also **creates the test data** (author, reader, tag, post, comment, review) that the other folders use. Run it first.

item.name: App is connected to the database

request.description: AC 1.1.4: the app reads counts from MySQL. Also starts a new run id, so usernames and titles are unique.
JpaRepository.save() inserts the User. The id comes from MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT. The password is stored as a BCrypt hash and never returned.
One transaction: load the author, find or create the tags, insert the post and its post_tags rows.

item.name: US 2.1 - Manage blog data through repositories
item.description:
**As an administrator, I want to manage blog data through repositories so that CRUD operations are automated and efficient.**

Acceptance criteria covered:
- AC 2.1.1 Repositories for User, Post, Comment, Tag and Review (CRUD for each)
- AC 2.1.2 Derived query methods (findByUsername, findByAuthorUsername, findByTagsName, existsBy..., countBy...)
- AC 2.1.3 @Query with JPQL and native SQL

Deletes are in the last folder ("Clean up"), so the test data stays available for the other stories.

item.name: US 2.2 - Pagination and sorting
item.description:
**As a reader, I want to view blog posts with pagination and sorting so that I can navigate large datasets easily.**

Acceptance criteria covered:
- AC 2.2.1 Pagination and sorting with Pageable (?page, ?size, ?sort), max size 100, sort-field whitelist
- AC 2.2.2 Paginated responses for posts and comments, and for **every other list** too (users, tags, tag usage, reviews, top rated, popular, summaries, search, audit log, keyset feed): without parameters each one returns page 0 with a default size and order
- AC 2.2.3 Performance: compare the deep OFFSET page with the keyset feed in the response times (seed the DB with the "seed" profile for real numbers)

US 3.1 - Data consistency (transactions)
item.description:
**As a developer, I want to ensure data consistency during post and comment updates so that no data loss occurs during concurrent transactions.**

Acceptance criteria covered:
- AC 3.1.1 @Transactional on create / update / delete
- AC 3.1.2 Propagation (REQUIRES_NEW audit log, MANDATORY tags) and isolation (REPEATABLE_READ stats)
- AC 3.1.3 Rollback verified: optimistic locking (409 on an old version) and a rejected post that leaves nothing behind

Run in order: the requests pass versions to each other.

item.name: Update post with the current version (200, version + 1)
Update post with the OLD version - lost update blocked (409)

request.description: A second editor who read the post before the first edit. Optimistic locking (@Version) refuses the write instead of silently overwriting.

item.name: The first edit is still there
Edit comment with the current version (200)
Edit comment with the OLD version (409)
Create post with a banned word - rejected and rolled back (400)

request.description: The new tag is created inside the transaction (MANDATORY), then the banned-word check fails. rollbackFor = ContentRejectedException undoes everything.

item.name: Rollback check - the new tag was NOT saved

request.description: Native query, not cached: reads straight from the database. size=100 so every tag is on the page.

exec: pm.test("no rejected post", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.content.map(p => p.title)).to.not.include("Rejected post " + pm.collectionVariables.get("run")));

item.name: Audit log kept the failed attempt (REQUIRES_NEW)

request.description: The audit row is written in its own transaction, so it survives the rollback of the post.

item.name: US 3.2 - Query optimization
item.description:
**As a database analyst, I want to optimize complex queries so that system response times are improved.**

Acceptance criteria covered:
- AC 3.2.1 Complex JPQL / native queries optimized (DTO projections, batch fetching, no N+1)
- AC 3.2.2 Indexes used by the frequent queries (status + created_at, author, FULLTEXT on title/content)
- AC 3.2.3 Response times: every request logs its time in the Postman console. Run with the seeded DB (`seed` profile, 50,000 posts) to compare with Docs/performance-report.md.

The time limits in the tests are generous smoke checks, not benchmarks.

US 4.1 - Caching
item.description:
**As a reader, I want to load frequently accessed posts faster so that the application feels responsive.**

Acceptance criteria covered:
- AC 4.1.1 Popular posts, posts, users and tags are cached (Spring Cache + Caffeine)
- AC 4.1.2 @EnableCaching config: each cache has its own size and TTL (see /api/cache-stats)
- AC 4.1.3 Invalidation after create/update: @CachePut / @CacheEvict, checked below with real writes
- AC 4.1.4 Improvement measured: compare the response time of the 1st (miss) and 2nd (hit) call in the Postman console

item.name: US 5.1 - Documentation
item.description:
**As a project contributor, I want to document all repository interfaces, queries, and caching mechanisms so that the application can be maintained easily.**

The written documentation is in README.md, Docs/repositories-and-queries.md, Docs/transactions.md and Docs/performance-report.md.
These requests check the live API documentation (springdoc OpenAPI + Swagger UI).

item.name: Clean up (US 2.1 - soft deletes)
item.description:
Deletes everything this run created. Run last.

Every delete is a **soft delete**: the row stays in MySQL with `deleted_at` set, and the API never shows it again.
- Deleting a post also soft-deletes its comments and reviews; deleting a user also soft-deletes their posts and the comments and reviews they wrote or received.
- Unique values only count live rows, so a deleted review, title, tag name or username can be used again (the "... again (201)" requests).

To see the kept rows: `SELECT post_id, title, deleted_at FROM posts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL;`

item.name: Review again after deleting (201, unique counts live reviews only)
Delete post (also soft-deletes its comments and reviews)
Get deleted post (404, cache was evicted)
Create a post with the deleted title again (201)
Deleted tag is gone from the tag list
Create the deleted tag name again (201)
Delete author (also soft-deletes their posts, comments and reviews)
Create a user with the deleted username and email again (201)
